newsitem.title: USA: Slim savings seen from CBOT-CME joint clearing.
newsitem.headline: Slim savings seen from CBOT-CME joint clearing.

text.p: A proposal to merge the clearing systems at Chicago's two futures exchanges may not be economically feasible, a study commissioned by the Joint Strategic Initiatives Committee has found, but committee members will continue to examine the issue.

A source close to the committee said the first part of a three-part study on common clearing showed that consolidating the hardware systems of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Chicago Board of Trade's clearing operations would actually cost money.
Merton Miller, executive director of the committee, declined to elaborate on the study, but said the first part determined that a merger of the two systems would provide slim initial savings.
"The hardware gains are there, but they are limited and they are small," Miller said in an interview.
He said the committee was still reviewing the first part of the study, which was finished last week.

Last year, the committee commissioned Electronic Data Systems Corp, an information technology company and consultant based in Plano, Texas, to study the costs and savings of merging CME and CBOT clearing operations.
The CBOT and the CME both said they were reviewing the study and had no comment.

The first part of the study studied costs and savings from consolidating CBOT and CME clearing hardware. The second part, to be released this summer, will focus on the cost-savings benefits of merging both clearinghouses' software, he said.

"We are moving on to the next stage to see if the software ...is more promising and then we'll also start the contentious issue of getting a governance system for common clearing," Miller said, referring to the third part of the study.
Miller said the third part would focus on ownership and stockholder issues if a separate clearinghouse is established.

While the CME manages its own clearinghouse, the CBOT's clearing system is managed by the Board of Trade Clearing Corporation (BOTCC), an independent entity from the exchange, which complicates bringing the clearing operation under one roof.
"It raises some issues," Miller said. "If it were just the two exchanges, that is one thing. If it is two exchanges plus the clearing corporation, that is more complicated."

The CBOT-CME Joint Strategics Initiatives Committee was formed in January 1996 to discuss consolidating back-office operations and procedures at the CBOT and CME to reduce duplicative costs for firms and traders.

The JSCI's common clearing subcommittee, which was formed in early 1997, will meet at the Futures Industry Association's annual meeting in Boca Raton, Florida, this week, several industry sources said.
